This is a synthetic infrastructure check. Find and read Anthropic's official Claude Code documentation overview page.

Constraints: use ONLY the WebSearch and WebFetch tools. Do not use any other tools (no Bash, no file reads/writes, no other agents).

Steps:
1. Use WebSearch to locate Anthropic's official Claude Code documentation overview page (it should be on an official Anthropic domain, e.g. docs.claude.com, code.claude.com, or docs.anthropic.com).
2. Use WebFetch on the page you found to confirm it is the official Claude Code overview and to read its actual page title. If WebFetch reports a cross-host redirect, call WebFetch again on the redirect URL and report the final URL.

Report back:
- The exact page title as it appears on the fetched page
- The final URL you actually fetched (after any redirects)
- Which tool calls you made (WebSearch query used, WebFetch URL(s)), and whether any failed
Do not guess: if a fetch fails, say so plainly rather than inferring the title.

I found the official Claude Code overview page, and the main thing to know is that it has moved to a new web address.

**Where the official docs are now**

Anthropic's GitHub repo for Claude Code points to its official documentation at code.claude.com/docs/en/overview. A third-party directory also says the official Claude Code documentation lives at code.claude.com/docs/en/. The old address, https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/overview, still shows up in search results with the same overview page.

**What the overview page says**

- **What it is:** A coding tool that can read your codebase, edit files, run commands and connect to your development tools. You can use it in the terminal, an IDE, a desktop app or the browser.
- **What you need to use it:** Most versions need a Claude subscription or an Anthropic Console account. The terminal version, VS Code and JetBrains also work with third-party providers.
- **Terminal:** On Linux you can also install with apt, dnf or apk (Debian, Fedora, RHEL and Alpine). Then go to your project folder and run `claude`. It asks you to log in the first time, unless you've set the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable and approve using that key.
- **VS Code:** Search for "Claude Code" in the Extensions view. After installing, open the Command Palette, type "Claude Code" and choose Open in New Tab.
- **Desktop app:** A separate app where you can review changes visually, run several sessions side by side, schedule recurring tasks and start cloud sessions. It's available for macOS and Windows.
- **Next step:** The page links to a Quickstart that walks you through a first real task, from exploring a codebase to committing a fix.

**Other official Anthropic resources**

- **Product page (claude.com/product/claude-code):** Suggests giving Claude a bug fix, a test or a migration that takes several days, and then checking its work from your terminal, IDE, Slack or the web. It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- **GitHub repo (github.com/anthropics/claude-code):** You can use it in your terminal or IDE, or tag @claude on GitHub.
- **Claude Platform docs (platform.claude.com/docs):** This is the main documentation site for Anthropic's API. It also links to Claude Code, calling it an agentic coding assistant in your terminal.
- **"How Anthropic teams use Claude Code" (PDF):** Examples from Anthropic's own teams. For instance, the security engineering team wrote half of all the custom slash commands in Anthropic's main shared codebase.

**One conflicting source**

The freeCodeCamp Claude Code Handbook tells readers to go to code.claude.ai and calls it Anthropic's official installation hub for Claude Code. That doesn't match the code.claude.com address on Anthropic's own GitHub repo, so I'd trust code.claude.com.

**Unofficial guides**

If you also want guides written by users, ClaudeLog covers practical tips, ways to get more out of the tool and community best practices. Tons of Skills keeps an organized list of the official docs on skills, plugins, agents, hooks, MCP, the command line and best practices.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content
